cohort: This review synthesizes findings from studies on infants and young children, focusing on microbial colonisation in the first three years of life, particularly the first hundred days and first year.
finding: Microbial dysbiosis in the gut and upper airway during the first years of life is strongly associated with the development, persistence, phenotypes, and severity of asthma, as well as recurrent viral infections.
mod_finding: Caesarean delivery is identified as one of the factors associated with early microbial dysbiosis, which is linked to an increased risk of asthma.
